description: Second-order linear non-homogeneous ODE ay'' + by' + cy = p(x): general solution y = y_c + y_p, plus the method-of-undetermined-coefficients table for guessing y_p's form from p(x) (polynomial, exponential, sinusoidal, and their products, each split by whether the associated root already appears in the characteristic equation). Ends with a three-part worked drill covering a polynomial RHS, an exponential RHS, and a polynomial-times-trig RHS.

lessons.title: y = y_c + y_p for ay'' + by' + cy = p(x)
solution_steps: \text{Find } y_c\text{, the general solution of the associated homogeneous equation } ay''+by'+cy=0.
\text{Find one particular solution } y_p \text{ of } ay''+by'+cy=p(x)\text{, whose form depends on the type of } p(x).

lessons.title: Particular-solution guessing table (method of undetermined coefficients)
lessons.statement_latex: \text{Let } h(x), g(x) \text{ denote polynomials of the same degree as the polynomial factor of } p(x), \text{ and } \lambda \text{ range over the roots of the characteristic equation.}
solution_steps: p(x)=f(x)e^{\alpha x} \text{ (}f(x)\text{ a degree-}n\text{ polynomial): if } \alpha \text{ is not a root} \implies y_p=h(x)e^{\alpha x}; \text{ if } \alpha \text{ is a simple root} \implies y_p=xh(x)e^{\alpha x}; \text{ if } \alpha \text{ is a double root} \implies y_p=x^2h(x)e^{\alpha x}

p(x)=k\sin\beta x \text{ or } k\cos\beta x: \text{ if } \beta i \text{ is not a root} \implies y_p=A\cos\beta x+B\sin\beta x; \text{ if } \beta i \text{ is a root} \implies y_p=x(A\cos\beta x+B\sin\beta x)

p(x)=f(x)\cos\beta x \text{ or } f(x)\sin\beta x: \text{ if } \beta i \text{ is not a root} \implies y_p=h(x)\cos\beta x+g(x)\sin\beta x; \text{ if } \beta i \text{ is a root} \implies y_p=x\big(h(x)\cos\beta x+g(x)\sin\beta x\big)

p(x)=ke^{\alpha x}\cos\beta x \text{ or } ke^{\alpha x}\sin\beta x: \text{ if } \alpha\pm i\beta \text{ is not a root} \implies y_p=e^{\alpha x}(A\cos\beta x+B\sin\beta x); \text{ if } \alpha\pm i\beta \text{ is a root} \implies y_p=xe^{\alpha x}(A\cos\beta x+B\sin\beta x)

p(x)=f(x)e^{\alpha x}\cos\beta x \text{ or } f(x)e^{\alpha x}\sin\beta x: \text{ if } \alpha\pm i\beta \text{ is not a root} \implies y_p=e^{\alpha x}\big(h(x)\cos\beta x+g(x)\sin\beta x\big); \text{ if } \alpha\pm i\beta \text{ is a root} \implies y_p=xe^{\alpha x}\big(h(x)\cos\beta x+g(x)\sin\beta x\big)
\text{Additivity: if } p(x)=f_1(x)+f_2(x) \text{ and } f_1,f_2 \text{ give particular solutions } y_{p_1}, y_{p_2} \text{ respectively, then } y_p=y_{p_1}+y_{p_2}.

lessons.title: Solve y'' - 2y' - 3y = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x (polynomial RHS)
solution_steps: \text{Homogeneous: } \lambda^2-2\lambda-3=0 \implies (\lambda+1)(\lambda-3)=0 \implies \lambda=-1 \text{ or } \lambda=3 \implies y_c=Ae^{-x}+Be^{3x}
\text{Ansatz: } y_p=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d \implies y_p'=3ax^2+2bx+c \implies y_p''=6ax+2b
\begin{cases}-3a=2\\-6a-3b=-5\\6a-4b-3c=3\\2b-2c-3d=0\end{cases} \implies \begin{cases}a=-\tfrac{2}{3}\\b=3\\c=-\tfrac{19}{3}\\d=\tfrac{56}{9}\end{cases}

lessons.title: Solve y'' + 3y' + 3y = 3e^{2x} (exponential RHS, complex-root complementary solution)
solution_steps: \text{Homogeneous: } \lambda^2+3\lambda+3=0,\ \Delta=3^2-4\cdot 3=-3 \implies \lambda=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}=-\frac{3}{2}\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i \implies y_c=e^{-\frac{3}{2}x}\left(A\cos\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}x+B\sin\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}x\right)
\text{Ansatz (}\lambda=2\text{ is not a root): } y_p=Ae^{2x} \implies y_p'=2Ae^{2x} \implies y_p''=4Ae^{2x}
4Ae^{2x}+3(2Ae^{2x})+3(Ae^{2x})=3e^{2x} \implies 13Ae^{2x}=3e^{2x} \implies A=\frac{3}{13}

lessons.title: Solve y'' - y' - y = x cos x (polynomial-times-trig RHS)
solution_steps: \text{Homogeneous: } \lambda^2-\lambda-1=0,\ \Delta=1-4(1)(-1)=5 \implies \lambda=\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{2} \implies y_c=Ae^{\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}x}+Be^{\frac{1-\sqrt5}{2}x}
\text{Ansatz (}\beta=1,\ i \text{ is not a root): } y_p=(ax+b)\cos x+(cx+d)\sin x
y_p'=(cx+a+d)\cos x+(-ax-b+c)\sin x
y_p''=(-ax-b+2c)\cos x+(-cx-2a-d)\sin x
y_p''-y_p'-y_p=x\cos x \implies (-2ax-2b+2c-cx-a-d)\cos x + (-2cx-2a-2d+ax+b-c)\sin x = x\cos x
\begin{cases}-2a-c=1\\-a-2b+2c-d=0\\a-2c=0\\-2a+b-c-2d=0\end{cases} \implies \begin{cases}a=-\tfrac{2}{5}\\b=-\tfrac{1}{5}\\c=-\tfrac{1}{5}\\d=\tfrac{2}{5}\end{cases}
